title: Does History Repeat Itself? – Prepositions of Time (English Grammar Lesson)
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

sentences.en: People often say history repeats itself… but does it really?
sentences.zh: 人们常说历史会重演……但真的会吗？

sentences.en: When we look back at the past, certain events feel strangely familiar.
sentences.zh: 当我们回顾过去时，某些事件会给人一种莫名的熟悉感。

sentences.en: Pandemics that spread across the world. Wars that change everything.
sentences.zh: 席卷全球的大流行病。改变一切的战争。

sentences.en: Economic crashes that seem to happen just when people feel most confident about the future.
sentences.zh: 经济崩盘似乎总是在人们对未来最有信心的时候发生。

sentences.en: Even though the details are different, the patterns can feel… repeated.
sentences.zh: 尽管细节有所不同，但这些模式却让人感觉……在重复。

sentences.en: Also, when we talk about history, time matters.
sentences.zh: 另外，当我们谈论历史时，时间很重要。

sentences.en: Not just what happened, but when it happened.
sentences.zh: 不仅在于发生了什么，还在于什么时候发生。

sentences.en: How specific we are, and how we describe time in English.
sentences.zh: 我们讲得有多具体，以及我们在英语中如何描述时间。

sentences.en: We talk about events in certain centuries, on particular days, and at exact moments that changed the world.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是某些世纪、特定日子里以及改变世界的精确时刻发生的事件。

sentences.en: So in today’s episode, we’ll do two things.
sentences.zh: 所以在今天的节目中，我们将做两件事。

sentences.en: First, I’ll give you a short and clear grammar lesson on prepositions of time: in, on, and at.
sentences.zh: 首先，我将为大家带来一堂简短明了的语法课，讲解时间介词：in、on 和 at。

sentences.en: Then, we’ll explore some big moments from history and ask whether history really does repeat itself.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们将探讨历史上的一些重大时刻，并探讨历史是否真的会重演。

sentences.en: As you listen, pay attention to how I use in, on, and at!
sentences.zh: 在听的时候，注意我是如何使用 in、on 和 at 的！

sentences.en: Prepositions of time show when something happens.
sentences.zh: 时间介词用来表示某事发生的时间。

sentences.en: In English, the most common ones are in, on, and at.
sentences.zh: 在英语中，最常见的介词是 in、on 和 at。

sentences.en: The key difference between these three prepositions is how specific the time is.
sentences.zh: 这三个介词之间的核心区别在于时间有多具体。

sentences.en: Use “in” when you are talking about large blocks of time or time that is not exact.
sentences.zh: 当你谈论大块时间或不确定的时间时，使用“in”。

sentences.en: Think of “in” as “inside a long period of time”.
sentences.zh: 把“in”想象成“在一个长时期之内”。

sentences.en: We use in with:
sentences.zh: 我们将 in 与以下内容连用：

sentences.en: Use “on” when the time is more specific and usually connected to a day.
sentences.zh: 当时间更具体且通常与某一天相关时，使用“on”。

sentences.en: We use on with:
sentences.zh: 我们将 on 与以下内容连用：

sentences.en: Use “at” when the time is very specific or exact.
sentences.zh: 当时间非常具体或确切时，使用“at”。

sentences.en: We use at with:
sentences.zh: 我们将 at 与以下内容连用：

sentences.en: Let’s start by talking about economic crashes, because I think this is one of the clearest examples people use when they say “history repeats itself”.
sentences.zh: 让我们从经济崩盘开始谈起，因为我认为这是人们在说“历史重演”时用得最清晰的例子之一。

sentences.en: The most famous example is the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 最著名的例子就是大萧条。

sentences.en: It began in the 1930s, but many historians argue that it started on October 29th, 1929.
sentences.zh: 它始于 20 世纪 30 年代，但许多历史学家认为它始于 1929 年 10 月 29 日。

sentences.en: This day is remembered as Black Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 这一天被称为黑色星期二。

sentences.en: That was at the start of the stock market collapse, when panic selling spread through Wall Street and confidence in the financial system disappeared almost overnight.
sentences.zh: 那是股市崩盘的开始，当时恐慌性抛售蔓延到华尔街，人们对金融系统的信心几乎在一夜之间消失了。

sentences.en: At the time, many people believed the economy would quickly recover.
sentences.zh: 当时，许多人相信经济会迅速复苏。

sentences.en: Instead, the crisis lasted for years. Businesses closed, banks failed, and ordinary people, normal people, suffered the consequences.
sentences.zh: 相反，这场危机持续了多年。企业倒闭，银行破产，普通人、寻常百姓承受了后果。

sentences.en: The 1930s were a decade marked by widespread unemployment, poverty, and economic instability across much of the world.
sentences.zh: 20 世纪 30 年代是一个以广泛的失业、贫困和世界大部分地区经济不稳定为特征的十年。

sentences.en: And the effects were not just economic, but social and political as well.
sentences.zh: 而且这些影响不仅是经济上的，也是社会和政治上的。

sentences.en: Now fast forward to a more recent event.
sentences.zh: 现在快进到一个更近的事件。

sentences.en: In 2008, the world experienced another massive financial shock.
sentences.zh: 2008 年，世界经历了又一次巨大的金融冲击。

sentences.en: Housing bubbles burst, major financial institutions collapsed, and governments were forced to intervene.
sentences.zh: 房地产泡沫破裂，主要金融机构倒闭，各国政府被迫干预。

sentences.en: At the height of the financial crisis, fear spread globally.
sentences.zh: 在金融危机最严重的时候，恐惧在全球蔓延。

sentences.en: Ordinary people were worried about their jobs, savings and futures.
sentences.zh: 普通民众都在担心自己的工作、积蓄和未来。

sentences.en: When we compare these two moments, the details are clearly different.
sentences.zh: 当我们比较这两个时刻时，细节显然是不同的。

sentences.en: The technologies were different. The financial systems are more complex now.
sentences.zh: 技术不同了。现在的金融系统更加复杂。

sentences.en: Governments responded more quickly in 2008 than they did in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 2008 年各国政府的反应比 20 世纪 30 年代更快。

sentences.en: But the underlying patterns look familiar.
sentences.zh: 但潜在的模式看起来很熟悉。

sentences.en: Excessive risk taking, overconfidence, lack of regulation, and a sudden loss of trust.
sentences.zh: 过度冒险、过度自信、缺乏监管以及信任的突然丧失。

sentences.en: Another area where history feels as if it’s repeating itself is pandemics.
sentences.zh: 历史感觉在重演的另一个领域是大流行病。

sentences.en: When a disease spreads rapidly, our reactions often follow very familiar patterns.
sentences.zh: 当疾病迅速传播时，我们的反应往往遵循非常熟悉的模式。

sentences.en: We usually see fear, confusion, denial, and eventually adaptation.
sentences.zh: 我们通常会看到恐惧、困惑、否认，最后是适应。

sentences.en: One of the most famous examples is the Spanish Flu.
sentences.zh: 最著名的例子之一就是西班牙流感。

sentences.en: It spread globally in 1918, at the end of World War I, when countries were already exhausted from the brutal war and healthcare systems were under huge pressure.
sentences.zh: 它在 1918 年第一次世界大战结束时在全球蔓延，当时各国已经饱受残酷战争的摧残，医疗系统承受着巨大的压力。

sentences.en: At the time, information moved slowly and many governments tried to downplay the danger.
sentences.zh: 当时，信息传递缓慢，许多政府试图淡化危险。

sentences.en: As a result, millions of people became infected before the seriousness of the situation was fully understood.
sentences.zh: 结果，在人们充分认识到局势的严重性之前，数百万人已被感染。

sentences.en: Now, compare that with a much more recent experience.
sentences.zh: 现在，把它与最近得多的经历进行比较。

sentences.en: In 2020, the world faced the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 2020 年，世界面临了 COVID-19 大流行。

sentences.en: Within months daily life changed dramatically.
sentences.zh: 在几个月内，日常生活发生了巨大变化。

sentences.en: Borders closed, travel stopped, and entire cities went into lockdown.
sentences.zh: 边境关闭，旅行停止，整座整座的城市进入封锁状态。

sentences.en: At the beginning of the pandemic, many people believed the disruption would be short term.
sentences.zh: 在大流行初期，许多人认为这种混乱将是短暂的。

sentences.en: But as weeks turned into months, it became clear that this was a long lasting crisis.
sentences.zh: 但随着数周变成数月，人们逐渐清楚地认识到这是一场持久的危机。

sentences.en: Despite the difference in medical technology and communication, again the patterns are similar.
sentences.zh: 尽管医疗技术和通讯手段有所不同，但模式再次相似。

sentences.en: In both periods, misinformation spread quickly.
sentences.zh: 在这两个时期，虚假信息都迅速传播。

sentences.en: People argued about restrictions and governments struggled to balance public health with economic survival.
sentences.zh: 人们就限制措施争论不休，政府则艰难地在公共卫生与经济生存之间寻找平衡。

sentences.en: I think wars are often used by people as the strongest evidence that history really does repeat itself.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们经常把战争当作历史确实会重演的最强有力证据。

sentences.en: Even though the world looks more modern and more connected and more advanced, the reasons that conflicts begin tend to sound very familiar.
sentences.zh: 尽管世界看起来更现代、联系更紧密、技术更先进，但冲突爆发的原因听起来往往非常熟悉。

sentences.en: If we look back, in the 20th century, many major wars started with a similar combination of factors.
sentences.zh: 如果我们回顾过去，在 20 世纪，许多重大战争都是由相似的因素组合引发的。

sentences.en: There was economic pressure, political instability, nationalism, and a fear of an external threat.
sentences.zh: 当时存在经济压力、政治不稳定、民族主义以及对外部威胁的恐惧。

sentences.en: Alliances formed, tensions rose over time, and eventually a single event on a specific day pushed countries into open conflict.
sentences.zh: 同盟形成，紧张局势随时间加剧，最终特定一天的一个单一事件将各国推向公开冲突。

sentences.en: Once fighting began, decisions made at critical moments determined how long wars lasted and how destructive they became.
sentences.zh: 一旦战斗打响，关键时刻做出的决定就决定了战争持续多久以及破坏性有多大。

sentences.en: Now, compare that with conflicts in the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 现在，把它与 21 世纪的冲突进行比较。

sentences.en: The names, the places and the technologies are of course different.
sentences.zh: 名字、地点和技术当然都不同了。

sentences.en: But again, the patterns often look the same.
sentences.zh: 但同样，这些模式往往看起来是一样的。

sentences.en: Long periods of tension build in the years before a war.
sentences.zh: 在战争爆发前的几年里，长期的紧张局势不断积聚。

sentences.en: Warning signs appear. And leaders insist conflict can be avoided.
sentences.zh: 警告信号出现了。而领导人们坚称冲突是可以避免的。

sentences.en: Until suddenly, on one particular morning, everything changes.
sentences.zh: 直到突然之间，在某一个清晨，一切都变了。

sentences.en: Missiles are launched at dawn. Borders are crossed at night and the world wakes up to another war that no one wanted.
sentences.zh: 导弹在黎明时分发射。边境在夜间被跨越，世界在又一场无人想要的战争中醒来。

sentences.en: What’s striking is how often people say the same things.
sentences.zh: 令人震惊的是，人们说的话竟然如此相似。

sentences.en: In the past, leaders claimed war was necessary for security.
sentences.zh: 在过去，领导人声称战争对安全是必要的。

sentences.en: In more recent times, they use almost identical language.
sentences.zh: 在更近的时期，他们使用几乎完全相同的语言。

sentences.en: And at the moment violence begins, the consequences are always felt most heavily by ordinary people.
sentences.zh: 而在暴力开始的那一刻，普通人受到的影响总是最重的。

sentences.en: Political and social movements are another area where the idea of history repeating itself feels very real.
sentences.zh: 政治和社会运动是历史重演感非常真实的另一个领域。

sentences.en: Across different countries and centuries, people rise up in protest or revolution for many of the same reasons.
sentences.zh: 在不同的国家和世纪中，人们出于许多相同的原因挺身而出进行抗议或革命。

sentences.en: Usually these reasons are connected to inequality, maybe injustice, and a feeling that the system, the politics, the economics no longer represents them.
sentences.zh: 通常这些原因与不平等、可能还有不公正有关，并且觉得体制、政治、经济不再代表他们的利益。

sentences.en: If we look back, major social movements often begin during periods of longterm pressure.
sentences.zh: 如果我们回顾过去，大型社会运动往往在长期压力的时期开始。

sentences.en: In times of economic hardship or political repression, frustration builds slowly.
sentences.zh: 在经济困难或政治高压时期，挫折感慢慢积聚。

sentences.en: For a while, nothing seems to change. Then suddenly, on a particular day, a protest, a speech, or a single incident becomes a turning point.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，似乎什么都没有改变。然后突然之间，在特定的一天，一场抗议、一次演讲或单一事件成为了转折点。

sentences.en: At that moment, a political or social movement is born.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，一场政治或社会运动诞生了。

sentences.en: We can see this pattern repeated again and again.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到这种模式一遍又一遍地重复。

sentences.en: Revolutions in the 18th and 19th centuries followed it.
sentences.zh: 18 和 19 世纪的革命遵循了它。

sentences.en: Civil rights movements in the 20th century followed it too.
sentences.zh: 20 世纪的民权运动也遵循了它。

sentences.en: In recent years, similar movements have emerged around the world.
sentences.zh: 近年来，世界各地涌现出类似的运动。

sentences.en: Different causes, different slogans, but the same structure.
sentences.zh: 不同的诉求，不同的口号，但结构是相同的。

sentences.en: Long-term pressure in the background, a triggering event on a specific day, and then rapid change at a critical moment.
sentences.zh: 背景中的长期压力，特定日期的触发事件，然后是关键时刻的迅速变化。

sentences.en: In the past, those in power often dismissed protestors as dangerous or unrealistic.
sentences.zh: 在过去，当权者经常把抗议者斥为危险分子或不切实际。

sentences.en: In the present, the same language is still used.
sentences.zh: 在当下，同样的语言依然在使用。

sentences.en: And the demands of protestors are often simple and repeated across history… fairness, dignity, and a voice.
sentences.zh: 而抗议者的诉求往往很简单，并在历史上不断重复……公平、尊严和话语权。

sentences.en: So after looking at economic crashes, pandemics, wars, and social movements, we come back to the original question, the title of this episode… Does history really repeat itself?
sentences.zh: 所以在审视了经济崩盘、大流行病、战争和社会运动之后，我们回到了最初的问题，也就是本期节目的标题……历史真的会重演吗？

sentences.en: If we compare events in different centuries, it’s clear that the world changes.
sentences.zh: 如果我们比较不同世纪的事件，很明显世界在改变。

sentences.en: Technology becomes more advanced, societies become more complex, and people right now have far more access to information than ever before.
sentences.zh: 技术变得更先进，社会变得更复杂，现在的人们比以往任何时候都能获得更多的信息。

sentences.en: What happened in the past is never repeated in exactly the same way.
sentences.zh: 过去发生的事情绝不会以完全相同的方式重演。

sentences.en: The details are always different. But when we look at patterns over time, the similarities are hard to ignore.
sentences.zh: 细节总是不同的。但当我们审视跨时间的模式时，相似之处很难让人忽视。

sentences.en: The same pressures build in the years before a crisis.
sentences.zh: 危机爆发前的几年里，同样的压力在积聚。

sentences.en: The same warnings are ignored. And then on a particular day, something triggers a chain of events that leads to dramatic change.
sentences.zh: 同样的警告被忽视了。然后在特定的一天，某件事引发了一连串事件，导致了戏剧性的变化。

sentences.en: At that moment, people often react with surprise, even though the signs were there.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，人们往往会惊慌失措，尽管迹象其实一直都在。

sentences.en: This suggests that history doesn’t repeat itself like a loop, but more like a rhythm.
sentences.zh: 这表明历史并非像循环一样重复，而更像是节奏。

sentences.en: Human behavior and emotions and decision making don’t change as quickly as technology does.
sentences.zh: 人类的行为、情绪和决策并不像技术那样变化得那么快。

sentences.en: So while events happen in different contexts, they often follow familiar paths.​
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管事件发生在不同的背景下，它们往往遵循熟悉的轨迹。

sentences.en: So here is today’s final thought. Does history really repeat itself?
sentences.zh: 所以这是今天的最后思考。历史真的会重演吗？

sentences.en: Maybe not exactly in the same way. The details change, the technology changes, the world looks very different, but I think patterns clearly appear over time.
sentences.zh: 也许不是以完全相同的方式。细节变了，技术变了，世界看起来大不相同，但我认为模式在随着时间推移清晰地显现出来。

sentences.en: Human behavior, fear, ambition, and mistakes seem to return again and again even in different historical periods.
sentences.zh: 人类的行为、恐惧、野心和错误似乎一次又一次地卷土重来，即使在不同的历史时期也是如此。

sentences.en: And throughout this episode I have been trying to demonstrate how to use English Prepositions of Time.
sentences.zh: 在整期节目中，我一直在试图演示如何使用英语时间介词。

sentences.en: We use “in” to talk about long general periods:
sentences.zh: 我们用“in”来谈论漫长的一般时期：

sentences.en: We use “on” for specific days and dates:
sentences.zh: 我们用“on”来表示具体的日子和日期：

sentences.en: And we use “at” for exact times and decisive moments:
sentences.zh: 我们用“at”来表示确切的时间和决定性的时刻：

sentences.en: As you listen to English in the future, pay attention to how native speakers talk about time.
sentences.zh: 当你将来听英语时，注意母语者是如何谈论时间的。

sentences.en: Notice when they choose in, on or at, and think about how specific the moment is.
sentences.zh: 注意他们何时选择 in、on 或 at，并思考这个时刻有多具体。

sentences.en: If you want to practice using English prepositions of time, try describing a historical event yourself using all three prepositions.
sentences.zh: 如果你想练习使用英语时间介词，试着用所有的三个介词亲自描述一个历史事件。

sentences.en: Talk about what happened in a certain period, what changed on a particular day, and what happened at a key moment.
sentences.zh: 谈谈某段时期内发生了什么，特定的一天发生了什么变化，以及关键时刻发生了什么。

sentences.en: And I’ll leave you with one final question.
sentences.zh: 最后我留给大家一个问题。

sentences.en: “If history really does repeat itself, what do you think will happen in the future?”
sentences.zh: “如果历史真的会重演，你认为未来会发生什么？”
